nodes.statement_short: Show $\triangleleft$ is trivial and $c\ast c=1_S$.

nodes.name: Encode the action
nodes.statement: Indeed, using (\ref{eq:nor1a}) we already know that $1_S \triangleleft h = 1_S$, for all $h \in H$. Let $f : H \to S$ be a map such that $ c \triangleleft h = f(h)$, for all $h \in H$. Then, $f$ is a unit preserving map since (\ref{eq:nor1a}) holds.
nodes.statement_short: Encode $c\triangleleft h$ as a unit-preserving map $H\to S$.

nodes.name: Action rule
nodes.statement: We will prove that $f (h) = c$, for all $h \in H$, and hence $\triangleleft$ is the trivial action. Indeed, $(ES1)$ tells us that $\triangleleft$ is a right action: the condition $c \triangleleft (g h) = (c \triangleleft g) \triangleleft h$ takes the form $f (g h) = f(g) \triangleleft h$, for all $g$, $h \in H$.
nodes.statement_short: (ES1) gives $f(gh)=f(g)\triangleleft h$.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: Assume, that there exists $g \in H$ such that $f (g) = 1_S$. Then we obtain that $f (g h) = 1_S \triangleleft h = 1_S$, i.e. $f (gh) = 1_S$, for all $h\in H$. Thus, $f$ is the trivial map, that is $c \triangleleft h = 1_S$, for all $h \in H$. Then, axiom $(ES2)$ applied for $s_1 = s_2 = s_3 = c$ implies that $ (c \ast c) \ast c = c \ast c$ and using $(ES7)$ we obtain $c = 1_S$, which is a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: If some $f(g)=1_S$ then the action is trivial to $1_S$, and (ES2), (ES7) force $c=1_S$.

nodes.name: Translate axioms
nodes.statement: Thus, $\triangleleft$ is the trivial action; it follows from $(ES1)$ that $\ast$ is a group structure on $S$ i.e. $c \ast c = 1_S$. Now, any normalizing map $ \triangleright : S \times H \to H$ is uniquely implemented by a map $D : H \to H$ such that $c \triangleright h = D(h)$, for all $h\in H$, and any normalized map $f : S \times S \to H$ is uniquely determined by an element $h_0 \in H$ such that $f (c, c) = h_0$. Now we can easily see that the compatibility conditions $(ES1)$, $(ES2)$, $(ES4)$ are trivially fulfilled, while $(ES3)$ is equivalent to the fact that $D$ is an endomorphism of $H$, axiom $(ES5)$ takes the equivalent form given by the right hand side of (\ref{eq:ind2aa}) while $(ES6)$ is the left hand side of (\ref{eq:ind2aa}).
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize by $(h_0,D)$ and translate (ES3),(ES5),(ES6) into $D$ automorphism and (44).

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: $(2)$ Let $(\ast, \triangleleft, \, \triangleright, \, f)$ and $(\ast', \triangleleft', \, \triangleright', \, f')$ be two group extending structures associated to $(h_0, D)$ and $(h'_0, D') \in {\mathcal T} (H)$. Then, $(\ast, \triangleleft, \, \triangleright, \, f) \sim (\ast', \triangleleft', \, \triangleright', \, f')$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{de:equiv1} if there exists a pair $(r, v)$ of unitary maps $r: S \rightarrow H$, $v: S \rightarrow S$ such that $v$ is a bijection on the set $S$ and the compatibility conditions (\ref{eq:p1}) - (\ref{eq:p4}) are fulfilled. Since $|S| = 2$ and $v$ is a unitary bijection we obtain that $v$ is the identity map on $S$. On the other hand, the unitary map $r: S \to H$ is given by an element $g \in H$ such that $r (c) = g$. Taking into account the construction of the group extending structures from (\ref{eq:ind2}) we can easily show that the compatibility conditions (\ref{eq:p1}) - (\ref{eq:p4}) take the equivalent form (\ref{eq:ind2bb}).
nodes.statement_short: Translate the equivalence of Definition 2.15 into (46).

nodes.name: Set up equivalence
nodes.statement: Let $(\ast, \triangleleft, \, \triangleright, \, f)$ and $(\ast', \triangleleft', \, \triangleright', \, f')$ be two group extending structures associated to $(h_0, D)$ and $(h'_0, D') \in {\mathcal T} (H)$. Then, $(\ast, \triangleleft, \, \triangleright, \, f) \sim (\ast', \triangleleft', \, \triangleright', \, f')$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{de:equiv1} if there exists a pair $(r, v)$ of unitary maps $r: S \rightarrow H$, $v: S \rightarrow S$ such that $v$ is a bijection on the set $S$ and the compatibility conditions (\ref{eq:p1}) - (\ref{eq:p4}) are fulfilled.
nodes.statement_short: Two structures from $(h_0,D)$, $(h'_0,D')$ are equivalent via unitary $(r,v)$.

nodes.name: v is the identity, r is an element
nodes.statement: Since $|S| = 2$ and $v$ is a unitary bijection we obtain that $v$ is the identity map on $S$. On the other hand, the unitary map $r: S \to H$ is given by an element $g \in H$ such that $r (c) = g$.
nodes.statement_short: $v=\mathrm{Id}_S$ and $r$ is given by $g=r(c)$.

nodes.name: Conditions become (46)
nodes.statement: Taking into account the construction of the group extending structures from (\ref{eq:ind2}) we can easily show that the compatibility conditions (\ref{eq:p1}) - (\ref{eq:p4}) take the equivalent form (\ref{eq:ind2bb}).
